sources.title: Proclamation No. 1334/2024, A Proclamation to Determine Public Holidays and Celebration of Public Holidays (English text, MetaAppz Ethiopian federal laws)
sources.said: 4. Celebrated National Holidays The following holidays are Celebrated National Holidays to be celebrated at the national level: September 11, New Year (Enkutatash) March 02, Adwa Victory Day May 01, International Workers’ Day May 05, Ethiopian Patriots’ Victory Day Governmental and Non Governmental institutions shall be closed for public service on the national public holidays prescribed under Sub-Articles (1-4) of this Article. 5. Memorial National Holidays … february 20, Ethiopian Martyrs’ Day, december 09, Ethiopian National Unity Day … Governmental and Non-Governmental institutions shall be open for public service on the National Public Holidays prescribed under Sub-Article (1) of this Article. 6. Religious Holidays The following Holidays are Religious Holidays to be celebrated at the National level: September 27, Meskel Holiday, Notwithstanding a change of date in a leap year, January 07, Christmas Holiday, January 19, Epiphany Good Friday, Easter, Mawlid, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Without prejudice to provisions of this proclamation and other laws Governmental and Non-Governmental institutions shall be closed for public service on the religious holidays prescribed under Sub-Articles (1-8) of this Article.

sources.title: Fana Media Corporation, Ethiopian Muslims Celebrate Eid al-Fitr Nationwide in Spirit of Unity and Joy (20 March 2026)

sources.title: Fana Media Corporation, President Taye Extends Eid al-Adha Greetings to Muslim Community (26 May 2026)
sources.said: President of Ethiopia Taye Atske-Selassie has extended warm greetings to the Muslim community on the occasion of the 1447th Eid al-Adha festival, which will be observed tomorrow, May 27, 2026.

sources.title: Fana Media Corporation, Ethiopian Muslims Mark Mawlid With Faith, Solidarity and Community Support (25 August 2026)
